purpose: Record four previously absent named watercourses that an IIRR watershed brief describes as tributaries of the Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape, without treating the brief as fish evidence or a surveyed hydrography layer.

source.title: Small Landscapes and Watersheds: Engaging local stakeholders in conservation
source.publicationDateNote: No publication date was visible in the retrieved pages; the URL upload folder is not treated as a publication date.

context.sourceReportedRelationship: The brief names Hiwasayan River, Maulawin River, Prensa Creek and Sisi Creek as four major tributaries of Maulawin Spring Protected Landscape in Guinayangan, Quezon.
context.namedLocalities: It describes an approximate Hiwasayan route from the protected landscape through named upland/lowland barangays to the coast at Arbismen and Ragay Gulf. It groups Maulawin River and the two creeks across central/coastal Guinayangan barangays without separate mapped reaches.
context.biology: A search of the 16-page PDF text for 'fish' returned no match. The document is watershed-management context, not a fish survey or occurrence source.

crosswalks.name: Hiwasayan River
crosswalks.sourceContext: The report estimates a 12 km route, says it begins in the MSPL strict-protection forest zone, describes it through upland and lowland barangays, and places its coastal exit at Arbismen into Ragay Gulf.
crosswalks.scopeDecision: Add one source-named river research lead. The reported approximate length and barangay sequence are not a traced centerline, surveyed reach, coordinate set, or boundary.

crosswalks.name: Maulawin River
crosswalks.sourceContext: Named as an MSPL tributary and grouped with Sisi and Prensa creeks in a source-described path through central/coastal barangays.
crosswalks.scopeDecision: Add one source-named river research lead; the shared route description does not delineate a channel. Keep distinct from Maulawin Spring and the Water District's Maulawin Itaas and Maulawin Ibaba spring-source entries.

crosswalks.name: Prensa Creek
crosswalks.sourceContext: Named as an MSPL tributary; the report groups its route with Maulawin River and Sisi Creek through central/coastal barangays.
crosswalks.scopeDecision: Add one source-named stream research lead; no individual route or channel geometry is inferred.

crosswalks.name: Sisi Creek
crosswalks.sourceContext: Named as an MSPL tributary; the report groups its route with Maulawin River and Prensa Creek through central/coastal barangays.
crosswalks.scopeDecision: Add one source-named stream research lead; keep it distinct from the barangay Sisi and the grouped Maulawin Itaas/ Ibaba spring-source locality. No individual route or geometry is inferred.

limitations: The IIRR brief is secondary watershed-management material; it is not a hydrographic survey or current feature registry.
The three Maulawin/Sisi/Prensa routes are described together and cannot be split into individual traced channels from this source.
The source-reported 12 km Hiwasayan length is approximate and does not justify generating a line or validating the entire river extent.
No fish names, aquatic occurrence data, current ecological condition, water safety, salinity, public access, legal fishing access, or reuse permission is established.
The protected-area and water-supply setting is context only; it does not mean these named watercourses are open to fishing.
nextAction: Seek primary DENR/PAMO or LGU hydrography for feature identity and route validation, then find independently reviewable, station-resolved fish evidence and item-specific reuse terms. Keep all four leads out of public species rows until those checks are complete.
